# Intake Brief: Review Queue depth notification is incorrect (AH-0MUDYTQ55002NUSJ)

## Headline

When the herdr worklist review queue is deep, the footer banner currently always
says "— audits will drain it". It must instead say "— focus on audits" while any
review item still lacks a current audit, and "Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')" once
every review item is audited.

## Problem statement

The herdr worklist shows a review-queue-depth banner when the root-only
`completed/in_review` count reaches `browseItemCount`. Today the banner copy is
fixed ("… — audits will drain it"), so it gives the same instruction whether
audits are still outstanding or the queue is fully audited and ready to ship.
The copy should reflect the actual audit state so the producer knows whether to
keep running audits or to ship.

## Users

- **Producer / sprint lead** — reads the banner to decide the next action.
  - *User story:* As a producer, when the review queue is deep and some items
    still need auditing, I want the banner to say "focus on audits" so I know
    audits are the drain. When every item in the queue has a current audit, I
    want the banner to say "Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')" so I know I can ship.
- **Downtime dispatcher / operator** — must be unaffected: the banner is
  display-only and never gates dispatch (WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. When the review queue is deep (root-only `completed/in_review` count ≥
   `browseItemCount`) **and** at least one root-level `in_review` item has an
   outstanding audit, the footer banner text reads exactly:
   `Review queue deep (<completed> of <browseItemCount> completed/in_review) — focus on audits`.
2. When the review queue is deep **and** no root-level `in_review` item has an
   outstanding audit, the footer banner text reads exactly:
   `Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')`.
3. "Outstanding audit" is determined by the existing audit-freshness semantics
   (`isAuditFresh` / `inReviewBucket`): an `in_review` item with no stored
   `auditedAt`, or whose stored audit is not current, counts as outstanding. A
   fresh, passed audit does not.
4. The banner remains display-only: it never disables downtime dispatch, never
   writes/clears `.herdr-downtime-disabled`, and does not change code-freeze
   banner behaviour or the `showHelpText` gate.
5. Automated tests assert the exact rendered banner text for both variants and
   for the boundaries (deep+outstanding → deep+none; deep → shallow), using the
   existing worklist render test seams.
6. All related documentation/code comments describing the banner are updated to
   the new copy and the outstanding-audit condition.

## Constraints

- **Source repository:** the banner is implemented in the **ContextHub** repo
  (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`), not in `AI_Hell`. This work item is tracked
  in the `AI_Hell` worklog (consistent with existing tooling work items such as
  AH-0MUDYHPPC008F7PV); implementation must target the ContextHub source tree.
- `browseItemCount` default 20, re-read live from settings (no restart).
- Root-only counting via `wl list --status completed --stage in_review
  --root-only --json` (same query as `fetchCompletedItemCount`).
- No new persistence mechanism; reuse existing fetch helpers where possible.
- Display-only; must not reintroduce the sprint-complete auto-disable
  (WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD RCA root cause A).
- Keep the change minimal: banner copy + the state needed to choose it.

## Existing state

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` renders the banner in the footer branch
  (~3596–3617): `const bannerText = \`Review queue deep${countDisplay} — audits will drain it\`;`
  where `countDisplay` = ` (<completed> of <browseItemCount> completed/in_review)`.
- `refreshSprintState()` (~4531–4546) calls `fetchCompletedItemCount()`
  (`packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` ~684) and sets
  `sprintComplete = count >= liveBrowseCount`. Only a count is retained —
  per-item audit state is not currently available to the banner.
- `fetchCompletedItemCount()` runs `wl list --status completed --stage in_review
  --root-only --json` and returns the item count. `wl list --json` items expose
  `stage`, `status`, `auditedAt`, `auditResult`, `fingerprint`, `updatedAt`
  (but not `currentFingerprint`).
- Audit freshness is centralised: `isAuditFresh(...)` in
  `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` (~306) and the audit-aware bucket predicate
  `inReviewBucket(...)` in `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` (~360–389). The
  audit-dispatch tier uses the same predicate.
- There are currently **no automated tests** covering the banner text or
  `refreshSprintState` — this gap must be closed.

## Desired change

- Extend the banner-state refresh (or add a sibling helper) so it knows whether
  any root-level `in_review` item has an outstanding audit, in addition to the
  deep-queue boolean.
- Select the banner copy from that state:
  - outstanding audits → `Review queue deep (<n> of <browseItemCount> completed/in_review) — focus on audits`;
  - none outstanding → `Ready to Ship (shortcut 'S')`.
- Add regression tests for both variants and the transition boundaries.
- Update the code comments that describe the banner to match the new copy and
  condition.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` — banner copy selection in the footer render
  branch (~3596–3617); `refreshSprintState` (~4531–4546); render-option plumbing
  for `sprintComplete` / `sprintCompletedCount` (~3359–3396, ~5893–5894).
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `fetchCompletedItemCount` (~681–699): extend
  or replace with an outstanding-audit-aware fetch of root `completed/in_review`
  items.
- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh` (~306) shared freshness
  predicate to reuse.
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — `inReviewBucket` (~360–389) audit-aware
  predicate (alternative reuse).
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.test.ts` — regression tests for both banner
  variants and boundaries.

## Related work

- **WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD** (ContextHub, done/deleted) — P2: replaced the
  sprint-complete auto-disable with the review policy; introduced the current
  "audits will drain it" banner copy.
- **WL-0MTHSHN5V008R5L0** (ContextHub, completed) — Auto-disable dispatching when
  sprint is complete; original sprint-complete banner ("Sprint Complete, hit S to
  ship").
- **WL-0MSI8H3HP000K0RG** (ContextHub, completed) — Allow `/skill:audit` on
  complete/in_review items without a valid audit; defines the "valid audit"
  (`isAuditFresh`) semantics reused here.
- **WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY** (ContextHub, completed) — Ship It shortcut ('S') with
  typed confirmation dispatching `/skill:ship release`.
- **WL-0MUDEJU9Z004UO2W** (ContextHub, blocked/plan_complete) — worklist
  pre-dialog ship gate + freeze-on-confirm integration (Ship Guard interaction).
- **WL-0MT2UQWOR007CYY9** (ContextHub, completed) — review-queue-depth gate for
  non-critical implement dispatch.
- **WL-0MU8808ZY0091JIA** (ContextHub, completed) — surface held gate in header
  (recent banner/header area change).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "outstanding audit" scope.** Defined as a **root-level**
  `in_review` item with no `auditedAt` or a non-current audit, matching the
  banner's root-only count. If child `in_review` items should also suppress the
  "Ready to Ship" copy, this must be confirmed (see Appendix).
- **Risk — fingerprint availability.** `wl list --json` does not return
  `currentFingerprint`, so `isAuditFresh` degrades to the 60 s time gate and a
  post-audit comment can falsely look stale, keeping "focus on audits" after
  audits complete. Mitigation: compute current fingerprints as the downtime
  worker/hydrator does, or add a purpose-built query.
- **Risk — misleading "Ready to Ship".** The 'S' ship shortcut is gated by the
  Ship Guard (live agent panes carrying this project's work-item IDs block
  shipping). "Ready to Ship" reflects audit state only; changing the guard is out
  of scope.
- **Assumption — condition structure preserved.** Only the deep-queue branch's
  copy changes; the banner still shows only when `isSprintComplete &&
  helpEnabled`.
- **Risk — missing test seams.** There is no existing banner test; the render
  pipeline is internal, so tests must use whatever seam the worklist suite
  already exercises, or expose a small pure helper for the copy decision.
- **Scope-creep risk:** do not touch the ship shortcut, Ship Guard, dispatch
  gating, or the queue-depth threshold. Capture extra opportunities as linked
  work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: What counts as an "outstanding audit"?**
  — Answer (research; no producer round): the freshness semantics already used
  across herdr — `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt, fingerprint,
  currentFingerprint)` returning false, or no stored `auditedAt`. Source:
  `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` (`isAuditFresh`), `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts`
  (`inReviewBucket`), and the audit-dispatch tier in `downtime-worker.ts`.
  **ASSUMPTION — root-only scope chosen to match the existing banner count;
  confirm at plan if child `in_review` items should also count.**
- **Q: Where does the banner code live?**
  — Answer (research): the ContextHub repository
  (`packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`); this work item is tracked in the AI_Hell
  worklog, consistent with other tooling work items filed there. Source: repo
  search + `wl` config (AI_Hell prefix `AH`, ContextHub prefix `WL`).
- **Q: Is 'S' the ship shortcut?**
  — Answer (research): yes — uppercase 'S' opens the typed-confirmation Ship It
  dialog that dispatches `/skill:ship release` (WL-0MSGG5N5Z0074TLY). Source:
  `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (`openShipItDialog`, `SHIP_IT_COMMAND`) and
  `packages/herdr/src/shortcuts.json`.
- *Interview style:* no producer interview round was required — the seed
  description plus repo/work-item search sufficed. The only open point is the
  outstanding-audit scope, recorded here as a documented assumption for producer
  confirmation.

# Enforce a per-item dispatch-attempt cap and flag items that exhaust it

**Work Item:** `WL-0MUKYEXMK0033MFK`

---

## Problem Statement

The herdr downtime dispatcher has no per-item attempt budget. Re-dispatch is bounded only by the success-marker TTL and the stage-advancement guard. Repeated non-terminal closes (observed as `agent-ended-no-terminal` / `audit-ended-no-result` during the 2026-09-28 review window) can therefore consume local-LLM slots across many idle cycles without any escalation. There is no machine-readable count of how many times the dispatcher has attempted an item, and no threshold at which the item is flagged for producer review.

**Concrete example:** During the 2026-09-28 review window, AI_Hell re-dispatched AH-0MUKMJRCI0002VBP for `implement` 3× in ~1h45m with the stage unchanged and a live pane still active — a per-item attempt cap would have stopped the loop and flagged the item for producer review.

## Users

- **Herdr operator:** Wants failing items to stop consuming dispatch slots and to be visible for manual triage.
- **Producer/reviewer:** Wants a flag on items that have exhausted their automatic dispatch budget, so they can triage and intervene.

## Users & User Stories

- **As a** Herdr operator, **I want** the downtime dispatcher to stop auto-dispatching an item once it has exceeded a configurable number of attempts for a given skill/kind, **so that** I can reclaim wasted compute and focus on items that are progressing.
- **As a** Producer/reviewer, **I want** items that exhaust their dispatch budget to be automatically flagged (`needsProducerReview = true`) with a clear reason, **so that** I can triage and decide whether to advance the stage, reassign, or close the item.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Attempt counter:** The dispatcher derives, from the rolling dispatch log, the per-item, per-kind count of dispatch attempts, including attempts whose pane closed non-terminally. No new persistent store is required if the existing log suffices; if a dedicated counter is needed, it must be fail-open (default 0).
2. **AC2 — Cap enforced:** Once the count reaches `maxAttempts` (configurable, clamped to a sane range, default documented), the item is excluded from further automatic dispatch of that kind.
3. **AC3 — Escalation:** On reaching the cap, the item is flagged `needsProducerReview = true` (with a distinct skip reason `attempt-budget-exhausted`) so it surfaces for human triage.
4. **AC4 — Stage advancement resets:** A stage advancement clears the budget for the previous kind (the item has demonstrably progressed and deserves a fresh attempt budget).
5. **AC5 — Neutral skip reason:** A budget-exhausted skip is a neutral reason, distinct from `no-candidate`, and never counts as a CLI-error strike.
6. **AC6 — Both dispatch paths:** The cap applies to BOTH the Herdr-list-head path and the coordination offer path.
7. **AC7 — Tests:** Unit tests cover:
   - (a) count below cap → eligible for dispatch
   - (b) count at cap → skipped with `attempt-budget-exhausted` reason
   - (c) flag set exactly once
   - (d) stage advancement resets the count
   - (e) corrupt/missing log → fail-open count of 0 (never block all dispatch)

## Constraints

- **Language:** TypeScript under `packages/herdr/src/`.
- **Non-breaking:** Must not weaken the existing duplicate-dispatch protections (`WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4`, `WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT`) — additive only.
- **Design:** The cap is a sequential **filter** on the ranked candidate sequence, not a new ranking algorithm.
- **Config:** `maxAttempts` should be configurable with a documented default (recommended: 3).

## Existing State

- Rolling dispatch log and marker readers in `downtime-log.ts`.
- `needsProducerReview` is already honoured as a global exclusion by the dispatcher, so setting it is sufficient to stop re-dispatch once flagged.
- The dispatcher uses two paths: (1) normal Herdr-head scan, and (2) coordination offer path — both need the cap applied.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — Rolling dispatch log reading; may need a `countAttempts(itemId, kind)` helper.
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Dispatcher selection logic; needs cap enforcement as a filter on both dispatch paths.
- `packages/herdr/src/config.ts` or equivalent — `maxAttempts` configuration (or use existing config mechanism).

## Related Work

- **WL-0MUBEZ6PE002WLP4** — RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches CRITICAL implement items (completed) — duplicate-dispatch prevention for same worktree.
- **WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT** — RCA: Downtime dispatcher re-dispatches same item (completed) — prior audit/plan-tier RCA.

## Risks & Assumptions

- The cap could block genuinely important items that legitimately need retries. *Mitigation:* Stage advancement resets the budget (AC4), and the cap is per-kind so a stage change opens a fresh budget.
- Config changes could accidentally raise the cap too high. *Mitigation:* Clamp to a sane range (e.g., min 1, max 10) with a documented default.

**Assumptions:**
- The rolling dispatch log at `.worklog/downtime-dispatches.log` contains entries for all dispatch attempts (both successful and non-terminal).
- The `needsProducerReview` flag, once set, is sufficient to exclude the item from dispatcher candidates.
- `maxAttempts = 3` is a reasonable default (based on observed patterns: 2-4 non-terminal retries before human intervention is warranted).

2. **Q:** Should the attempt counter be per-kind (per skill) or global per item? — **Answer (agent recommendation, per description):** Per-kind (per skill), as stated in the goal. This allows an item to progress through different skills without the budget for one skill being consumed by retries in another.

# Herdr: Drain sessions before switching to cheap mode

> When the herdr extension chooses to switch the proxy to cheap mode due to
> inactivity, it first waits until the active session count falls to the number
> of slots available in cheap mode. No new work items are dispatched until this
> requirement is met and the proxy has been switched to cheap. If an interactive
> command is given while draining, the switch is cancelled and the time is reset.
> The inactive time is set to 15 minutes.

## Problem statement

When the herdr mode-switch worker detects operator inactivity, it switches the
llama-proxy from fast (3-slot cloud-backed pool) to cheap (2-slot local-first
pool) mode. Currently this switch happens immediately once the idle threshold
is met and the proxy reports idle. This can interrupt in-flight operator work
that happens to be using a slot at the moment of the switch, and it can allow
more active sessions than the cheap pool can sustain (up to 3 in fast mode,
only 2 in cheap).

## Users

- **Operator running the herdr worklog plugin + llama-proxy** -- wants the proxy
  to drop to cheap mode based on their absence, but only after active work has
  naturally subsided to fit within the cheap pool.

User story:

- *As an operator, when I stop issuing agent-route commands through the herdr
  plugin for the idle window, I want the proxy to drain active sessions down to
  the cheap pool size before switching -- so I do not lose in-flight work and
  the cheap pool has capacity. If I return (issue a command), I want the process
  to cancel and reset.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Drain state:** when the idle threshold is met and the proxy reports
  idle, the mode-switch worker enters a **draining** state instead of switching
  immediately. It periodically checks whether the active session count (busy
  slots) has fallen to <= the cheap mode slot budget (2, i.e.
  `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS` free slots).
- [ ] **Dispatch pause during drain:** while in the draining state, the downtime
  dispatcher does **not** dispatch new work items. Existing in-flight work
  continues; the idle gate prevents new panes from spawning.
- [ ] **Drain completion:** once the proxy reports sufficient free slots (>= 2
  free), the drain ends and the proxy switches to cheap mode immediately.
- [ ] **Drain cancellation:** if an operator issues an agent-route command while
  draining, the drain is cancelled, the switch-to-cheap is abandoned, and the
  idle timer resets to "active now" (the proxy stays fast).
- [ ] **No redundant switching / no hammering:** skip when the persisted mode
  already matches the target; 409 treated as no-op; single-flight; at most one
  switch per state change.
- [ ] **Fail-closed everywhere:** endpoint failures, timeouts, and ambiguous
  payloads yield no switch; the worker stays in its current mode.
- [ ] **Idle threshold changed:** the default `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` is
  changed from 60 minutes to 15 minutes.
- [ ] **Tests:** unit tests cover -- drain state entry/exit, dispatch pause,
  operator-command cancellation, threshold change, all existing fail-closed
  paths unchanged. Full project suite green.

## Constraints

- The cheap mode slot budget is 2 slots (`DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS`). The
  drain condition is `freeSlots >= 2`.
- Draining must not kill in-flight work -- it only prevents *new* dispatches.
- The fast direction (operator command --> mode=fast) is unaffected; only the
  cheap idle switch path changes.
- The existing idle-clock reset mechanism (`lastOperatorCommandAt`) is reused
  for drain cancellation.
- Fail-closed remains the safe default at every boundary.

## Existing state

- The mode-switch worker (`mode-switch-worker.ts`) already tracks operator
  activity, polls `/llama/local/status` for idle evaluation, and switches to
  cheap on idle.
- The downtime worker (`downtime-worker.ts`) already controls dispatch based on
  the idle gate (`evaluateIdle`).
- The cheap mode slot budget is `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2` (parent
  WL-0MT9F67Y3008S0PR).
- The default idle threshold is `DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 3_600_000`
  (60 minutes).

## Desired change

Add a **draining** sub-state to the mode-switch worker's idle-to-cheap path:

1. **Entry:** After the idle threshold is met and the proxy reports idle, enter
   the drain state instead of switching.
2. **Polling during drain:** Each tick, check whether `freeSlots >= 2`. If so,
   switch to cheap and exit drain. If not, continue draining.
3. **Dispatch signal:** While in drain state, signal to the downtime worker to
   pause new dispatches.
4. **Cancellation:** If `onOperatorCommand()` fires during drain, exit drain
   immediately, reset the idle clock, and keep the proxy in fast mode.
5. **Default threshold:** Change `DEFAULT_MODE_SWITCH_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS` from
   3,600,000ms (60 min) to 900,000ms (15 min).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` -- Add draining state, drain logic,
  cancel on operator command, threshold constant change
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts` -- Drain state tests, cancel
  tests, dispatch-signal tests
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` -- Respect drain signal from mode-switch
  worker to pause dispatch
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` -- No change (threshold constant lives in
  mode-switch-worker, settings re-reads it per tick)

## Related work

- **WL-0MT9F67Y3008S0PR** -- Per-slot operator gate for cheap switch (completed)
- **WL-0MSN3FWV5008KQE9** -- Activity-gated proxy mode switching (completed)
- **WL-0MU6MXCZZ007ZXT9** -- Leader-only cheap switching (completed)
- **WL-0MU4MKVR4005WPBJ** -- Idle-trigger sources (completed)
- **WL-0MT1EE3S7005DJ1F** -- Tests: mode-switch worker core (completed)
- **WL-0MT1EEHQI002MOVT** -- Implement: mode-switch worker core (completed)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** Adding a drain state introduces a new state machine transition path.
  **Mitigation:** Keep the drain logic simple -- poll free-slots each tick,
  cancel on command. Reuse existing single-flight and fail-closed mechanisms.
- **Risk:** Race between operator command and slot freeing during drain. If both
  happen simultaneously, the operator command path takes priority -- the drain
  cancels and the idle clock resets, so the proxy stays fast. This is the
  correct user-facing behaviour.
- **Assumption:** The downtime worker can receive a signal from the mode-switch
  worker about the drain state. This is implemented via a callback on the
  mode-switch worker or a shared holder method (index.ts already uses the
  `modeSwitchHolder` pattern for the worker reference).
- **Assumption:** The "number of slots available in cheap mode" is the constant
  `DOWTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`.
- **Assumption:** Process restart during drain is safe -- the idle clock already
  resets to "active now" on construction (fail-safe: proxy stays fast until a
  fresh full idle window passes).
- **Scope control:** Making the drain threshold configurable is a follow-up
  opportunity, not in scope for this work item.
- **Scope control:** No change to the fast-switch path (operator command -->
  mode=fast); only the cheap idle-switch path gains drain semantics.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

This intake was completed without additional questions -- the work item
description provided sufficient detail to draft a clear brief.

# Problem Statement

`implement.py finish` runs only the pytest test suite because `_detect_test_tooling()` prefers pytest whenever the repo contains pytest-style test files. This silently ignores the canonical full suite declared in `.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands`, which for ContextHub is `npm --silent test -- tests/cli` and `npm --silent test -- tests/unit`. As a result, the finish gate never runs the vitest suite, creating a false sense of test coverage.

# Users

- **AI agents** running `/skill:implement` — the finish step's test gate must exercise the project's real full suite so that a push to dev is properly validated.
- **The herdr downtime worker** — auto-dispatches implement sessions; relies on finish's test gate being accurate.

# Acceptance Criteria

1. **`implement.py finish` honours `.pi/test-config.json` `suiteCommands` when present.** The test step uses the declared command list as the primary source and does not fall back to convention detection (pytest/npm/node) when `suiteCommands` is set.
2. **`run_tests()` in `implement.py` delegates to `full_suite_commands()` from the test skill.** The function resolves suite commands in the same order as `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`: extension file first, then convention detection.
3. **Changed-file scope (`scope="changed"`) is preserved.** When the test skill's changed-file selector is available and applicable, `implement.py` uses it; when unavailable (e.g. custom `suiteCommands` not introspectable), it falls back to the full suite with a logged warning.
4. **The fix is backward-compatible for repos without `suiteCommands`.** Repos that rely on convention detection (pytest-only, npm-only, node-only) continue to work as before, with the test skill's own convention detection replacing `implement.py`'s duplicate logic.
5. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.** All existing tests in both `implement.py` and the test skill must pass after the refactor.

# Constraints

- The change must not break repos that already have `suiteCommands` but use a different tooling mix (e.g. pytest + npm).
- No new external dependencies — reuse the existing import of `full_suite_commands` from the test skill.
- The `IMPLEMENT_TEST_COMMAND` env-var override retains highest precedence (unchanged).

# Existing State

- `_detect_test_tooling()` in `implement.py` checks: pytest → npm → repo-script → unity.
- `run_tests()` in `implement.py` branches on the detected tooling and runs only that suite.
- `full_suite_commands()` in `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` checks `suiteCommands` first, then conventions.
- The test skill's `changed_scope_commands()` is already imported (as `_changed_scope_commands`) but only used for pytest-specific subset selection.
- ContextHub's `.pi/test-config.json` declares: `["npm --silent test -- tests/cli", "npm --silent test -- tests/unit"]` — both are npm/vitest commands.

# Desired Change

Make `implement.py`'s `run_tests()` delegate to `full_suite_commands()` for the full suite, and to `changed_scope_commands()` (when available) for changed-file scope, matching the test skill's resolution order exactly.

# Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `run_tests()`, `_detect_test_tooling()`, `_has_pytest_suite()`, `_has_test_script()`
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `full_suite_commands()`, `changed_scope_commands()` (reference only)

# Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep risk:** This fix only addresses `implement.py`'s `run_tests()` function. Other consumers of `_detect_test_tooling()` (if any outside the test step) should be audited, but scope is limited to the finish test gate.
- **Assumption:** `_detect_test_tooling()` is only called from `run_tests()` and has no other callers in the implement skill. If it does, those callers need separate review.
- **Risk:** Changing the detection order may alter which repo-scope commands are selected in `changed_scope` mode for repos with `suiteCommands` + pytest. However, `changed_scope_commands()` in the test skill already returns `None` when `suiteCommands` is present (since it's not introspectable), so the fallback is always the full suite — the same behaviour as before (just now logged explicitly rather than silently).
- **Risk:** The test skill's `full_suite_commands()` is imported conditionally (in the try/except block). The fix must preserve the existing graceful degradation: when the test skill is partially installed, the full suite still falls back to convention detection.

# Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

No clarifying questions needed — the bug is self-evident from the code and the `.pi/test-config.json` declaration.

# Related Work

- WL-0MU1EWMHN000YUCG (Invalidating an audit) — the item from which this bug was discovered.
- SA-0MSTMYE79006NA61 — Feature 2: test skill honours `suiteCommands`.
- F2 AC4 — `full_suite_commands()` is the single source of truth for suite-command resolution.
- WL-0MSGQ64N2006TQB2 (implement.py worktrees lack node_modules) — related implement/test integration issue.

# Improve pane auto-close logic (WL-0MUMCZAC40058HCC)

## Problem statement

The current pane auto-close logic (controlled by `paneCloseEnabled`) is closing panes that should remain open. Since the default has been changed to `false`, the feature is currently inert — but when enabled, the classification logic needs improvement to avoid false-positive closes.

## Background

- **WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS** — "Investigate why completed plan/intake sessions are not closed on completion" — established the pane-close scheduler and reaper infrastructure.
- **WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN** — "Log all dispatches and auto close all completed dispatch panes, except implement" — created the pane-lifecycle classifier.
- The auto-close feature is now **disabled by default** (`paneCloseEnabled: false`) until the classification logic is improved.

## Current issues

The classification logic in `pane-lifecycle.ts` and `pane-close-reaper.ts` has been observed to close panes prematurely in certain scenarios:

1. **Intake panes** — May close before the operator has a chance to answer questions (when `needsProducerReview` is true but the state hasn't propagated).
2. **Plan panes** — May close before the producer has reviewed the output.
3. **Agent panes with long-running operations** — May be classified as idle when they are actually working but temporarily silent.
4. **Race conditions** — The pane-lifecycle monitor and the reaper may both attempt to close the same pane.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — No false-positive closes.** Pane auto-close must never close a pane where the operator might still need to interact (e.g. awaiting producer review, actively working, or has live child processes).
- **AC2 — Producer-review guard is robust.** A pane with `needsProducerReview=true` on its item must never be auto-closed, regardless of idle time or agent state.
- **AC3 — Active-agent detection is improved.** Pane-lifecycle classification must use additional signals beyond simple idle timeouts — e.g. recent file modifications, active network connections, or live child processes.
- **AC4 — Idempotent closes.** The reaper and the lifecycle monitor must not race; a pane can be closed at most once, with the outcome logged idempotently.
- **AC5 — Configurable grace period.** Add a `paneCloseGracePeriodMinutes` setting (default 5 minutes) — no pane is eligible for close within N minutes of its first dispatch, giving the agent time to start working.
- **AC6 — Better logging.** Every close decision includes a detailed reason with the full state snapshot (agent state, idle duration, item stage, needsProducerReview flag, child processes).
- **AC7 — Tests.** Table-driven tests for every classification path, including negative tests for the scenarios that previously caused false-positive closes.

## Key files

- `packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.ts` — Classification logic
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.ts` — Reaper orchestration
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-scheduler.ts` — Scheduling and defaults
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.ts` — Logging schema

# Stop closing/reaping panes (WL-0MUN72Y7Q0058JP7)

## Problem statement

The herdr worklog plugin's **scheduled pane-close reaper** (Mechanism A) automatically closes pi panes that it classifies as inactive. It is enabled **by default** and, because it enumerates panes with the workspace-global `herdr pane list` and does not filter by owner, a reaper instance running for one project can close panes belonging to **another project's workspace/window**. Operators want automatic pane-closing to be **off by default** and, when explicitly enabled, confined to its own project.

## Users

Primary user: a **herdr operator** running one or more worklog-enabled projects side-by-side and reading agent output in those panes.

- As a herdr operator, I want automatic pane-closing to be disabled by default, so that no agent pane disappears unless I explicitly opt in.
- As a herdr operator running several projects, I want an enabled reaper to only ever touch panes belonging to its own project, so that a reaper in project A cannot close a pane in project B.
- As a herdr operator who *does* want auto-close, I want to enable it via settings as before, with the guarantee that it stays within my project.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Off by default.** `DEFAULT_PANE_CLOSE_ENABLED` is `false` and `defaultSettings.paneCloseEnabled` is `false`. On a machine with no `paneCloseEnabled` override, `paneCloseReaperDue(...)` returns `false` / `runScheduledPaneClose(...)` is a complete no-op with **zero** close calls, and the worker never invokes the reaper.
- **AC2 — Workspace/project scoping.** When `paneCloseEnabled` is explicitly `true`, the reaper only evaluates panes whose project root matches the reaper's own project root (`cfg.cwd`). A pane belonging to any other project/workspace is excluded **before** classification and is never closed or sent to `closePane`.
- **AC3 — Fail-closed scope resolution.** `herdr pane list` parsing captures each pane's `cwd` (and/or `workspace_id`), and the scope decision is a pure, unit-testable function. A pane with missing/unknown `cwd` is treated as **out of scope** and skipped (never closed).
- **AC4 — Testing/validation.** Automated tests cover: default-disabled no-op; same-project pane eligible; cross-project pane skipped; missing-`cwd` pane skipped; and a regression test proving a reaper configured for project A never closes a pane whose `cwd` is project B.
- **AC5 — Documentation.** `packages/herdr/README.md` (pane-closure section and settings table) and the relevant settings doc comments are updated to state that auto-close is off by default and is project-scoped, with the setting to re-enable it.
- **AC6 — Related documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC7 — Full suite green.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Do not modify the operator's global config**: `~/.config/herdr/worklog-plugin.json` is left untouched; the operator applies their own local preference (Q3 answer).
- **Keep the capability**: operators who explicitly set `paneCloseEnabled: true` must still get auto-close — this is a default + scoping change, not a removal.
- **Fail-closed by design**: any ambiguity about a pane's owning project results in *no* close.
- **No behaviour removals beyond scope**: the pure reaper classification rules (marker, idle-threshold, never-close guards) are unchanged by this item.

## Existing state

- The reaper is wired into the downtime-worker tick in `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` (config gate ~L1834-1840, invocation ~L5557+), cadence `PANE_CLOSE_REAPER_INTERVAL_MS` = 60 s.
- `DEFAULT_PANE_CLOSE_ENABLED = true` (re-enabled by commit `b39dab9e` / WL-0MUMEJHT9004EQPI); `DEFAULT_PANE_CLOSE_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MINUTES = 0`; grace 5 min.
- With idle at 0, the only live close path is the `</end_session>` marker at the end of the final assistant message.
- Mechanism B (`pane-lifecycle.ts` dispatch monitor) is disabled (`PANE_LIFECYCLE_MONITOR_ENABLED = false`, WL-0MUMEKDK0008LKH8), so this reaper is the sole auto-close path.
- `createHerdrReaperDeps` lists **all** panes via `herdr pane list` and `parseHerdrPaneCloseList` currently discards the `cwd`/`workspace_id` fields that herdr returns, so no scoping is possible today.
- Evidence of cross-project impact: `projects/tce-main-street/.worklog/pane-close-ledger.jsonl` recorded `idle-threshold` and `dead-agent` closes on 2026-09-29, including panes in the operator's `w2V` window; some rows lack a `reasonSnapshot`, indicating a stale plugin build running older defaults.

## Desired change

1. Flip `DEFAULT_PANE_CLOSE_ENABLED` (and `defaultSettings.paneCloseEnabled`) to `false`.
2. Carry each pane's `cwd`/`workspace_id` through `parseHerdrPaneCloseList` → `ParsedHerdrPane` → `PaneStatus`.
3. Add a pure project-scope predicate to the reaper that compares the pane's project root with the reaper's `cfg.cwd` (path-boundary aware, e.g. `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub` matches `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub/packages/herdr` but not `/home/rgardler/projects/ContextHub-other`). Inject the scope root via `ReaperOptions`/`ReaperDeps` so the predicate is unit-testable without real herdr I/O.
4. Skip out-of-scope panes before classification; never close them.
5. Add the tests (AC4) and docs (AC5/AC6).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-scheduler.ts` — flip `DEFAULT_PANE_CLOSE_ENABLED` to `false`; keep the gated no-op path.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — `defaultSettings.paneCloseEnabled = false` and update the doc comment.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-herdr.ts` — capture `cwd`/`workspace_id` in `HerdrPaneCloseRecord`, `ParsedHerdrPane`, and `PaneStatus`; expose the scope fields to the classifier.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.ts` — add the pure project-scope predicate and skip out-of-scope panes in `runReaper`.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — pass `cfg.cwd` (project root) as the reaper scope when invoking `runScheduledPaneClose`/`runPaneCloseReaper`.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-reaper.test.ts`, `pane-close-herdr.test.ts`, `pane-close-scheduler.test.ts`, `settings.test.ts` — AC4 coverage.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — settings table + pane-closure section (AC5).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — leader scope.** The downtime worker leader is machine-wide, so only the leader's project runs the reaper. With auto-close off by default this is moot; when an operator enables it, their project's panes may not be reaped if another project holds leadership. Mitigation: document the behaviour; broader leader/scope design is out of scope for this item.
- **Risk — missing `cwd`.** Older herdr versions or non-pi panes may omit `cwd`; the fail-closed skip prevents accidental closes (may under-close). Acceptable.
- **Assumption.** `cfg.cwd` passed to `runPaneCloseReaper` is the project root (verified: `targetCwd` in `index.ts`, and each project has its own `pane-close-ledger.jsonl`).
- **Scope-creep risk.** A stale plugin build running old defaults was observed; the operator declined a stale-build guard (Q2 option c). Recorded as a follow-up candidate rather than expanding this item.

## Related work

- **WL-0MUMCZAC40058HCC** — Improve pane auto-close logic to avoid closing panes that need to stay open (bug, completed). Direct predecessor; established the false-positive-close problem.
- **WL-0MUMEJHT9004EQPI** — Improve Mechanism A idle timeout algorithm and re-enable auto-close (feature, completed). Re-enabled auto-close (commit `b39dab9e`), which this item reverses at the default level.
- **WL-0MUMEKDK0008LKH8** — Reconsider and disable Mechanism B (dispatch-monitor) pane auto-close (task, completed).
- **WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS** — Investigate why completed plan/intake sessions are not closed on completion (established the reaper infrastructure).
- **WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN** — Log all dispatches and auto close all completed dispatch panes, except implement (created `pane-lifecycle.ts`).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What is the desired end state?" — Answer (operator): **flip the shipped default to off** (`DEFAULT_PANE_CLOSE_ENABLED = false`), so no panes are auto-closed unless explicitly enabled. Source: interactive reply.

# Bug — Audit immediately invalidated after completion

## Problem statement

When an audit passes, the herdr selection list immediately shows the work item as having an "out of date" (stale) audit. The root cause is that `currentFingerprint` is never computed or included in the `wl list` JSON output, so the fingerprint-based freshness check in `isAuditFresh` always falls back to the fragile 60-second timestamp gate. Any post-audit metadata change (comment, sync, assignee update) bumps `updatedAt`, making valid audits appear stale within seconds.

**Concrete example:** WL-0MUIB7D30009KG00 ("herdr stage filters hide in-progress items") completed a passed audit with `fingerprint: a0796548e6989b53cc51a824d3fa8aae7b0cc9eba255665dc043298eadf65b19`, but `currentFingerprint` is always `null` in `wl list` output. The herdr selection list therefore shows the audit as stale (bucket 5: "passed audit, stale") instead of fresh (bucket 6).

## Users

- **Herdr downtime worker (auto-dispatch):** Incorrectly re-dispatches audits for items that already have valid, content-unchanged audits.
- **Operators viewing the herdr selection list:** See "stale audit" indicators on recently-audited items, causing confusion and unnecessary audit re-runs.
- **Producers reviewing work items:** May see stale audit warnings that delay release decisions.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **`wl list` output includes `currentFingerprint`** — The `wl list --json` command computes and includes a `currentFingerprint` field for every work item in its output.
2. **`currentFingerprint` reflects description content** — The fingerprint is a SHA-256 hex digest of the item's description field (the same content used to generate audit fingerprints). The computation must be deterministic and consistent across runs.
3. **Herdr correctly shows fresh audits** — Items with a valid, content-unchanged audit show as "fresh" (bucket 6 in the in_review sort) in the herdr selection list, even if `updatedAt` was bumped by non-semantic changes after the audit.
4. **All project tests pass** — No regressions in existing tests; new tests cover the `currentFingerprint` computation and its effect on audit freshness.

## Constraints

- Change must be confined to the `wl list` command's output path (`src/commands/list.ts` and its helpers).
- The fingerprint must match the audit fingerprint format (SHA-256 hex string) to be compatible with the existing `isAuditFresh` fingerprint comparison.
- No schema changes required — `currentFingerprint` is computed at read time, not stored.

## Existing state

- `packages/shared/src/icons.ts` — `isAuditFresh()` compares `fingerprint` vs `currentFingerprint` as the primary gate; falls back to 60-second time gate when either is missing.
- `src/commands/list.ts` — Outputs `fingerprint` from the stored audit result, but never computes `currentFingerprint`.
- `packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts` — `normalizeItem()` reads `currentFingerprint` from the raw JSON output (always `null`).
- `packages/herdr/src/grouping.ts` — `inReviewBucket()` calls `isAuditFresh()` with `currentFingerprint` (always `null`), causing the stale fallback.
- `src/audit.ts` — Audit fingerprints are extracted from audit text via `Audit content fingerprint: <sha256-hex>`. The description content is hashed by the AI agent during the audit run.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/commands/list.ts` — Compute `currentFingerprint` and include it in the JSON output.
- `src/commands/helpers.ts` — `computeCurrentFingerprint(description: string): string` helper (SHA-256 hex digest of description).
- `src/commands/list.test.ts` (or equivalent) — Tests for `currentFingerprint` computation and output.

## Risks & assumptions

1. **Fingerprint format mismatch** — The `currentFingerprint` must match the SHA-256 hex format used by audit fingerprints. If the AI agent hashes additional metadata (e.g., title, timestamps), the comparison will always fail. Assumption: the agent hashes only the description text.
2. **Performance** — Computing SHA-256 per item in `wl list` output is trivial for small repos but should be measured for large worklog databases. Risk is low.
3. **Scope creep** — Other commands (`wl show`, `wl next`) may also need `currentFingerprint`. Scope is `wl list` only; other commands are follow-ups.

# Child 2: Fix same-timestamp merge from invalidating audits via updatedAt churn

Parent: WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO (Invalidating an audit).

## Problem statement

`mergeSameTimestampItems` in `packages/shared/src/sync.ts:~L423` sets `merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString()` whenever local and remote have the same `updatedAt` but different content. This causes an unbounded timestamp advancement on repeated syncs, invalidating previously-passing audits.

The audit-freshness rule (`database.ts:644`, WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5: `auditedAt >= updatedAt`) then treats those items as edited-after-audit, causing passing audits to read as stale.

## Users

- **Developers using `wl sync`:** Sync should converge without advancing timestamps unboundedly.
- **Herdr downtime dispatcher:** Should not re-dispatch items that were recently audited but invalidated only by timestamp churn from sync.
- **Producers:** An audited item must retain its audit freshness across sync operations.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `mergeSameTimestampItems` only bumps `updatedAt` when the merge actually changed a user-visible field; converges without bumping when the merged result equals one side.
- [ ] Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` synced repeatedly converge with no unbounded timestamp advancement; existing audit freshness preserved.
- [ ] Regression test: a genuine semantic edit after audit still invalidates freshness (existing behaviour preserved).
- [ ] Existing re-sort / sync / audit tests pass; full suite green.

## Constraints

- Surgical change in `packages/shared/src/sync.ts` only. No schema migration.
- Preserve existing merge semantics for content resolution; only skip the timestamp bump when the merged result equals one side.
- Check sibling: WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA (re-sort updatedAt churn) — fix here must not conflict; note interaction in a comment.

## Key files

- `packages/shared/src/sync.ts:~L423` — `mergeSameTimestampItems`
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts:644` — `isAuditNotReadyFresh`

## Related work

- WL-0MU2O8AQ8000ASDO (parent: Prevent audit invalidation by non-semantic operations)
- WL-0MTH7G2O1004BHN5 (freshness rule — preserve for semantic edits)
- WL-0MTWU4XGP001GDEA (sibling re-sort fix)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Sync conflict risk:** Preventing `updatedAt` bumps may affect conflict resolution if both sides have divergent content. **Mitigation:** Preserve the existing merge semantics for content resolution; only skip the timestamp bump when the merged result equals one side.
- **Assumption:** The merge logic that compares local/remote content is sufficient to determine whether the merged result equals one side.,

# Dispatcher only dispatches work from the current sprint

## Problem statement

The downtime dispatcher currently dispatches work that is **not** displayed in the current sprint view. It consumes a Herdr head whose window is a fixed `30` (not the view's `browseItemCount`), and when that head yields no dispatchable candidate it **extends the window by up to 30 items** (`fetchExtendedHerdrItems` / `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX`) and dispatches candidates that the operator cannot see in the sprint view (`f-s-s` → `/wl`). The dispatcher must restrict **non-critical** dispatch to exactly the items the sprint view renders, and no-op when nothing in that view is dispatchable. Critical items remain eligible as a bounded safety escape hatch.

## Users

- **Operator / producer** — curates the sprint by what the default worklist shows (`browseItemCount`, plus the always-shown mandatory set). They need the dispatcher to act only on work they can see, so they are never surprised by out-of-view dispatch.
- **Downtime worker** — must not spend compute (agent panes, tokens) on backlog items that are hidden from the sprint view.
- **Dispatched agents** — should only be started for work that is visible in the current sprint.

Example user stories:

- *As an operator*, I want the downtime dispatcher to only start work that is visible in my sprint view, so that I retain control over what gets worked on.
- *As an operator*, when my sprint view holds nothing dispatchable, I want the dispatcher to no-op rather than scan hidden backlog, so that out-of-view items are never picked up.
- *As an operator*, I want a critical item to remain dispatchable even when the non-critical window is full, so a release blocker is never starved by the visible list.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Sprint-view-aligned dispatch window.** Both dispatcher selection paths — the check-in offer path (`computeMostImportantItem`) and the direct dispatch path (`dispatchDowntimeWork`) — pass the live per-root `browseItemCount` (clamped to the supported `1–50` range, the same setting and clamp the TUI uses) to `getHerdrListHead`. The candidate head therefore equals exactly the set rendered by the sprint view (`f-s-s` → `/wl`), including the mandatory set (`critical` ∪ completed/`in_review`) that is always shown regardless of count. Verification: unit tests assert `getHerdrListHead` is called with the effective `browseItemCount` on both paths, and a live settings change is re-read per dispatch cycle.

2. **No non-critical out-of-view dispatch.** The out-of-window extension (`fetchExtendedHerdrItems`, called at `downtime-worker.ts:3518` and `:4173`) never surfaces non-critical candidates. Either the extension is removed, or it is restricted to `priority === 'critical'` candidates. In both cases a non-critical item beyond the sprint view is never dispatched. Verification: the starvation regression introduced by WL-0MU6UL3GQ0015AA5 (mandatory set fills the window; the only dispatchable item is a non-critical out-of-window item) is **updated** to assert `no-candidate` (NOP) rather than a dispatch.

3. **NOP when the sprint view has no dispatchable work.** When every item in the sprint view is filtered by an existing safety gate, or the view is empty, the dispatcher reports the existing terminal reason (`no-candidate`, `review-queue-hold`, `code-freeze`, `fresh-audit-skip`, `audit-in-flight`, `audit-host-saturated`, `in-flight-hold`, or `wl-error`) and never falls back to a second ranking or an out-of-view non-critical scan. Verification: tests assert the terminal reason is derived only from in-view flags and that no second head lookup is performed for non-critical work.

4. **Critical items remain dispatchable.** All `critical` items are mandatory in the sprint view (fetched by `fetchMandatorySubsets` and always included by `selectWorkItems`), so they are always in-window; the existing `selectCriticalFirstCandidates` critical-first escalation still lets a critical item bypass the non-safety filters (dispatched-marker, review-queue hold). If a critical-only out-of-window escape hatch is retained, it must only ever yield `critical` candidates. Verification: a test asserts a critical item in the head still dispatches while every non-critical item is filtered; and, if the extension is retained, that it returns zero non-critical items.

5. **Existing safety gates preserved.** All dispatch-time gates remain unchanged and are still applied as sequential filters: scheduled-prompt, code-freeze, producer-review, dispatched-marker, free-slot minimums, active-audit single-flight, audit-host saturation, freshness/recency, CAS claim, and spawn. Verification: the existing gate tests continue to pass unmodified.

6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. In particular `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` states the new contract (dispatcher considers only the sprint-view window; empty/un-dispatchable view ⇒ NOP; the extended window is removed/restricted for non-critical work) and supersedes the WL-0MU6UL3GQ0015AA5 "extended dispatch window" wording.

7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Single ranking path.** No second ranking is introduced. Ordering remains `fetchNextItems` → `selectWorkItems` → `regroupWorkItems`; safety gates stay filters, not a fallback ordering.
- **Supersedes WL-0MU6UL3GQ0015AA5 AC1/AC4.** That completed item added the extension to prevent a 31-hour starvation incident. This item deliberately reverses the non-critical part of that behaviour; the starvation regression test must be updated explicitly (never silently deleted), and the risk recorded (see Risks).
- **`browseItemCount` semantics.** Clamped `1–50`; read live from settings per worklog root; per-root, not machine-wide.
- **Fail-open preserved.** A head-lookup CLI failure still resolves `{ok:false}` (strike / keep entry), never a panic; an empty view resolves the existing no-candidate path.
- **No regressions to TUI rendering.** The worklist keeps rendering exactly `browseItemCount`-bounded output (plus mandatory items).
- **No new persistence mechanism** and no changes to the coordination-file schema.

## Existing state

- **Sprint view** = default worklist (`f-s-s` → `/wl`): `fetchNextItems(browseItemCount)` → `selectWorkItems(…, browseItemCount)` → `regroupWorkItems(…)`. It always shows the mandatory set (all `critical` + all completed/`in_review`) plus `browseItemCount − mandatory` "others". `browseItemCount` default `20` (`packages/herdr/src/settings.ts:139`), clamped `1–50`.
- **Dispatcher head** = `getHerdrListHead(cwd, limit?)` → `fetchNextItems(limit ?? 30)` (`packages/herdr/src/index.ts:901`) — i.e. it defaults to a **fixed 30-item window**, not the view's `browseItemCount`.
- `computeMostImportantItem` (`downtime-worker.ts:3358`) and `dispatchDowntimeWork` (`:4148`) call `getHerdrListHead(cwd)` with **no limit**, so both use the default 30. Both already receive a `browseItemCount` value (parameter / `opts.browseItemCount`).
- **Out-of-window extension** = `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` (`downtime-worker.ts:2436`), bounded by `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX = 30` (`:292`); called at `:3518` (offer path) and `:4173` (direct path). Returned items are passed straight into `dispatchFromHerdrList` / `findOfferIn`, so **any** candidate (not just critical) can be dispatched from outside the view.
- Extension tests live in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` (`fetchExtendedHerdrItems — window extension primitive` and the extended-window describes, ~`:9693–9841`).

## Desired change

- Pass the live `browseItemCount` to `getHerdrListHead` in both dispatch paths, so the head equals the rendered sprint view; keep a sane fallback only when no limit is supplied.
- Remove the non-critical out-of-window extension (preferred), or restrict it to `critical` candidates only (the operator's chosen escape hatch). All critical items are already mandatory in the view, so a critical-only extension is normally inert and acts purely as a defensive safety net.
- Preserve `selectCriticalFirstCandidates` critical-first escalation and every existing safety gate.
- Update `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` (and any package README wording) to the new sprint-view-only contract.
- Update the WL-0MU6UL3GQ0015AA5 starvation regression test to assert the new NOP behaviour.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Pass `browseItemCount` to `getHerdrListHead` at `:3358` (`computeMostImportantItem`) and `:4148` (`dispatchDowntimeWork`); remove/restrict the `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` calls at `:3518` and `:4173`, and the helper (`:2436`) / `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX` (`:292`) if removed outright.
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts` — `getHerdrListHead` dep (`:901`): honour the caller-supplied `browseItemCount` limit (retain the fallback only for callers that pass none).
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.test.ts` — Replace the extended-window/fetchExtendedHerdrItems suites with sprint-view-only regression tests; update the starvation regression (WL-0MU6UL3GQ0015AA5) to expect `no-candidate`.
- `packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts` — Assert `getHerdrListHead` is called with the effective `browseItemCount` on the offer/leader paths.
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — Rewrite the "Extended dispatch window" section and the ranking-contract paragraph to state the sprint-view-only contract; record the supersession of WL-0MU6UL3GQ0015AA5.
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — Update any dispatch-window wording to match.

## Related work

- **WL-0MU6UL3GQ0015AA5** (completed) — *[downtime] Dispatch window can starve: Herdr head cap can exclude the only dispatchable item*. Introduced `fetchExtendedHerdrItems` / `DOWNTIME_DISPATCH_EXTEND_MAX`. **Directly superseded** by this item for non-critical work.
- **WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2** (completed) — *Dispatcher consumes Herdr selection list head (supersedes wl next unification)*. Parent of the above; established the "dispatcher == Herdr list head; gates are filters" contract this item refines.
- **WL-0MTHSHN5V008R5L0** (completed) — *Auto-disable dispatching when sprint is complete*. Background on the "sprint" concept and `browseItemCount`.
- **WL-0MTTSWC1X005P4VD** (completed) — reconciled the sprint-complete banner onto the live review-queue-depth signal.
- **WL-0MUL2IZLF002S9X5** (completed) — *Dispatches filter axis in the worklist*.
- **WL-0MSGSE15000746F7** (completed) — `f-s-s` returns to the default browse view (the sprint view referenced here).
- **WL-0MTMPIQBE001J41P** (completed) — *Remove coordination entry expiry; validate eligibility at dispatch time*.

#
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **WL-0MS3AN04T002O3OG** – GitHub issue number display in Herdr plugin detail view (completed)
- **WL-0MT3IA41F0074CWN** – Docs & observability for critical-first tier (completed)
- **WL-0MSDT8X1V003206G** – When filtering by stage, show all open work items in that stage (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `packages/herdr/README.md` — matched: 0mtk1ilm2009qyb2, 0mtmpiqbe001j41p, 0mu6ul3gq0015aa5, ac1, ac4 (+355 more)
- `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` — matched: 0mthshn5v008r5l0, 0mtk1ilm2009qyb2, 0mtmpiqbe001j41p, 0mttswc1x005p4vd, 0mu6ul3gq0015aa5 (+333 more)
- `CLI.md` — matched: accept, accepted, act, active, add (+261 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Starvation risk (accepted).** Restricting non-critical dispatch to the sprint view reintroduces the failure mode WL-0MU6UL3GQ0015AA5 fixed: if all visible items are blocked and the only dispatchable item lies beyond `browseItemCount`, the dispatcher no-ops. *Mitigation:* the view is operator-controlled — raising `browseItemCount` (up to 50) or clearing a blocker widens the dispatchable set; the critical-first escalation guarantees release blockers are never windowed out. The operator explicitly accepted this trade-off (Q2 answer B).
- **`browseItemCount` mismatch is the real bug.** Today the head uses `30` while the view uses `browseItemCount` (default `20`), so even without the extension the dispatcher can act on up to 10 items the operator cannot see. Aligning the head to `browseItemCount` is therefore required, not optional.
- **Scope-creep risk.** A "critical-only extension is inert" observation may tempt implementers to add a bespoke critical bypass; keep the change minimal and reuse the existing critical-first path. Any genuinely new capability discovered while implementing becomes a separate child/linked work item, not extra scope here.
- **Assumption (Q3 = A):** everything displayed in the sprint view is dispatchable — `critical` items, completed/`in_review` audit work, and ordinary "other" work.
- **Assumption (Q1 = A):** the dispatch window tracks the live `browseItemCount` setting, not a fixed constant.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1: What exactly defines the dispatch-eligible set?** The rendered view is capped by the live `browseItemCount` (default 20); the dispatcher head was fixed at 30.
  - Options: (A) use the live per-root `browseItemCount` as the head limit so dispatch == rendered view; (B) keep a fixed 30-item head, only remove the extra extension; (C) other.
  - **Answer (operator, interactive reply): (A).** Source: interactive reply. Final accepted answer: use the live per-root `browseItemCount` (clamped 1–50) as the dispatcher head limit.
- **Q2: How should the starvation risk be handled?** Strict sprint-view-only reintroduces the 2026-09-18 starvation mode fixed by WL-0MU6UL3GQ0015AA5.
  - Options: (A) accept strict sprint-view-only and mitigate operationally via `browseItemCount`; (B) keep a critical-only escape hatch, all non-critical dispatch sprint-view-only; (C) keep an extension but warn; (D) other.
  - **Answer (operator, interactive reply): (B).** Source: interactive reply. Final accepted answer: keep a critical-only escape hatch; all non-critical dispatch is sprint-view-only. Research note: because `fetchMandatorySubsets` always includes every `critical` item, all critical items are already mandatory in the view, so this escape hatch is expected to be a defensive no-op in normal operation (recorded as an assumption/risk above).
- **Q3: What remains dispatchable within the view?** The view always contains `critical` items and completed/`in_review` items, not just "others".
  - Options: (A) everything displayed (critical, in_review audits, ordinary work); (B) only non-review work; (C) other.
  - **Answer (operator, interactive reply): (A).** Source: interactive reply. Final accepted answer: everything displayed in the sprint view is dispatchable.

Audit remediation — root cause of remaining dropped keypresses found and fixed

Producer rejection: "We are still missing keystrokes when typing fast."

Root cause: the tick gate stops background sync/refresh while a form is open, but it cannot stop the PTY from COALESCING several keystrokes into a single stdin data event during fast typing. Both FormState.handleInput and ShipItDialogState.handleInput only accepted a single character (key.length === 1) and silently returned none for any multi-character chunk, discarding every character in it. Reproduced with a focused test: handleInput('hello') left the field empty.

Fix:
- New pure, dependency-free module packages/herdr/src/key-input.ts exports splitKeypresses(), a shared raw-stdin-chunk tokeniser. It keeps escape sequences intact as one token (CSI arrows / PageUp-Down / Ctrl+Enter / bracketed-paste markers, SS3, Alt-Meta) and returns every other code point as its own key, so no bytes are dropped.
- FormState.handleInput (form-dialog.ts) and ShipItDialogState.handleInput (ship-it-dialog.ts) now run each chunk through splitKeypresses() and apply every key in order, returning the first terminal result (submitted/cancelled/paste/cut). Single-key callers are unchanged.
- The typing gate (isInputActive + createGatedTick) remains; it addresses sync/refresh contention, while the tokeniser addresses the residual fast-typing loss.

Tests (all green):
- key-input.test.ts (15): tokeniser unit coverage incl. mixed chunks and incomplete CSI remainder.
- form-dialog.test.ts (+8): coalesced chunks append every char, printable-before-escape, submit on trailing Enter, Backspace/Tab inside a chunk, bracketed paste.
- ship-it-dialog.test.ts (+3): 'ship' in one chunk appends fully, 'ship' submits, Backspace in a chunk.
- worklist.test.ts (+2): fast-typing chunk simulation across a skipped tick for FormState and ShipItDialogState.

Full packages/herdr suite: 2968 tests pass. Root build (tsc) clean.
